original_value: The issues of identity authentication and privacy protection of individuals in body area network (BAN) systems have raised much concern in past few years. To address the challenges of privacy protection in wireless BAN, an image encryption algorithm has been proposed recently by Wang et al. The encryption algorithm utilized two 1D chaotic maps to generate sub-chaotic matrices which are combined to perform encryption. The algorithm has good statistical encryption performance. However, a cautious inquiry finds that it has some underlying security defects. This paper evaluates the security of the Wang et al. encryption algorithm to show that it is totally breakable under proposed cryptanalysis and hence infeasible for privacy protection in BAN. It has been shown that the plain-image data can be recovered without any prior knowledge of secret key and plain-text. Furthermore, this paper also suggests an improved encryption scheme using secure hash algorithm SHA-512 for one-time keys and a 4D hyperchaotic system to subdue the security insufficiencies of the algorithm under study. The simulation results and analysis demonstrate that the improved image encryption scheme has excellent encryption quality, plain-image sensitivity, and resistance to possible cryptanalytic attacks.

result.paraphrase: Concerns over identity authentication and privacy protection for individuals in body area network (BAN) systems have grown in recent years. To tackle privacy issues in wireless BAN, Wang et al. recently proposed an image encryption algorithm. Their method uses two 1D chaotic maps to create sub-chaotic matrices, which are then combined for encryption, and it shows strong statistical encryption performance. However, careful examination reveals some inherent security flaws. This paper assesses the security of Wang et al.’s algorithm and demonstrates that, under the proposed cryptanalysis, it is completely breakable and therefore unsuitable for privacy protection in BAN. It also shows that the plaintext image can be recovered without any prior knowledge of the secret key or plaintext. In addition, this paper proposes an enhanced encryption scheme that employs the SHA-512 secure hash algorithm for one-time keys and a 4D hyperchaotic system to address the security weaknesses of the algorithm under review. Simulation results and analysis indicate that the improved image encryption scheme offers excellent encryption quality, strong plaintext sensitivity, and resistance to potential cryptanalytic attacks.
